content.shloka:
Maasaanaam kaartikah shreshtho devaanaam madhusoodanah |
Ashramaanaam grihasthah cha vedaanaam saama eva cha ||
content.meaning: Among all months, Kartik is the best; among all deities, Madhusudana (Vishnu) is the greatest; among all ashramas, the householder life is foremost; and among all Vedas, the Sama Veda is supreme.
content.transliteration:
Māsānāṁ kārtikaḥ śreṣṭho devānāṁ madhusūdanaḥ |
Āśramāṇāṁ gṛhasthaś ca vedānāṁ sāma eva ca ||

content.shloka: Kartik Maas (October-November) is considered the holiest month in the Hindu calendar. It is dedicated to Lord Vishnu and is also known as Damodara Maas, after a pastime of baby Krishna being bound by Mother Yashoda.
content.meaning: During this month, devotees perform special vratas, offer deepa daan (lamp donation), take early morning baths in sacred rivers, worship Tulsi, and observe strict spiritual discipline. The merit of all spiritual activities is multiplied during Kartik.
content.transliteration: Kartik Maas (October-November) is considered the holiest month in the Hindu calendar. It is dedicated to Lord Vishnu and is also known as Damodara Maas, after a pastime of baby Krishna being bound by Mother Yashoda.

content.shloka:
Na kaartika samo maaso na krita yuga samam yugam |
Na veda sadrisham shaastram na tirtham gangayaa samam ||
content.meaning: There is no month equal to Kartik, no age equal to Satya Yuga, no scripture equal to the Vedas, and no pilgrimage equal to the Ganga.
content.transliteration:
Na kārtika samo māso na kṛta yuga samaṁ yugam |
Na veda sadṛśaṁ śāstraṁ na tīrthaṁ Gaṅgayā samam ||

content.shloka: Key observances of Kartik Maas: 1) Lighting a ghee or sesame oil lamp daily at Tulsi plant and in temples. 2) Taking bath before sunrise (Prabhata Snaana). 3) Reading Bhagavata Purana and singing Damodarashtakam. 4) Observing Kartik Ekadashi vratas. 5) Performing Tulsi Vivah on Dwadashi after Devutthani Ekadashi.
content.meaning: The lighting of lamps (deepa daan) during Kartik is especially powerful. It is believed that a single lamp lit in the month of Kartik destroys the darkness of ignorance accumulated over many lifetimes.
content.transliteration: Key observances of Kartik Maas: 1) Lighting a ghee or sesame oil lamp daily at Tulsi plant and in temples. 2) Taking bath before sunrise (Prabhata Snaana). 3) Reading Bhagavata Purana and singing Damodarashtakam. 4) Observing Kartik Ekadashi vratas. 5) Performing Tulsi Vivah on Dwadashi after Devutthani Ekadashi.

content.shloka:
Deepadaanam pradaasyaami kaartike keshava priya |
Sarva paapa vinirmuktah vishnu lokam sa gacchati ||
content.meaning: I shall offer lamps in Kartik, which is dear to Lord Keshava. One who does so is freed from all sins and attains the abode of Vishnu.
content.transliteration:
Dīpadānaṁ pradāsyāmi kārtike keśava priya |
Sarva pāpa vinirmuktaḥ Viṣṇu lokaṁ sa gacchati ||

content.shloka: The tradition of lighting lamps in Kartik has deep spiritual significance. The lamp represents divine knowledge that dispels the darkness of ignorance. Ghee lamps are offered at temples, tulsi plants, rivers, and on peepal trees.
content.meaning: Sesame oil lamps are especially recommended during Kartik Maas. Devotees place them near temples, in front of Tulsi, on riverbanks, and in public places where they can illuminate paths for others. This act of selfless illumination carries immense spiritual merit.
content.transliteration: The tradition of lighting lamps in Kartik has deep spiritual significance. The lamp represents divine knowledge that dispels the darkness of ignorance. Ghee lamps are offered at temples, tulsi plants, rivers, and on peepal trees.

content.shloka:
Om deepajyotih parabrahma deepajyotir janaardanah |
Deepo me harimu paapam deepa jyotir namo namah ||
content.meaning: The light of the lamp is the Supreme Brahman, the light of the lamp is Janardana (Vishnu). May the lamp destroy my sins. Salutations to the divine light of the lamp.
content.transliteration:
Om dīpajyotiḥ parabrahma dīpajyotir janārdanaḥ |
Dīpo me harimu pāpaṁ dīpa jyotir namo namaḥ ||

content.shloka: How to perform Deepa Daan: 1) Use earthen lamps (diyas) with cotton wicks. 2) Fill with ghee or sesame oil. 3) Light the lamp at sunset, facing east or north. 4) Chant the above mantra while lighting. 5) Place the lit lamp near Tulsi, temple, or a sacred spot. 6) Never blow out the lamp — let it extinguish naturally.
content.meaning: It is believed that during Kartik, Lord Vishnu rests in the ocean of milk (Kshirsagar). The lamps offered by devotees illuminate His celestial chamber and please Him immensely. Offering lamps for the entire month of Kartik is equal to performing a thousand Ashwamedha Yajnas.
content.transliteration: How to perform Deepa Daan: 1) Use earthen lamps (diyas) with cotton wicks. 2) Fill with ghee or sesame oil. 3) Light the lamp at sunset, facing east or north. 4) Chant the above mantra while lighting. 5) Place the lit lamp near Tulsi, temple, or a sacred spot. 6) Never blow out the lamp — let it extinguish naturally.

content.shloka:
Prabhate kaartike maasi snaanam yah kurute narah |
Sarva teertha phalam tasya labhyate naatra samshayah ||
content.meaning: The person who takes an early morning bath during the month of Kartik obtains the merit of bathing in all sacred pilgrimage sites. There is no doubt about this.
content.transliteration:
Prabhāte kārtike māsi snānaṁ yaḥ kurute naraḥ |
Sarva tīrtha phalaṁ tasya labhyate nātra saṁśayaḥ ||

content.shloka: The practice of early morning bath (Prabhata Snaana) during Kartik is one of the most important observances. Devotees wake up during Brahma Muhurta (approximately 4:30 AM) and bathe in rivers, ponds, or at home with cold water.
content.meaning: This early morning bath is not merely physical cleansing — it is a spiritual purification. The pre-dawn hours of Kartik are charged with divine energy, and water at this time is considered sacred, as all holy rivers are believed to be present in it.
content.transliteration: The practice of early morning bath (Prabhata Snaana) during Kartik is one of the most important observances. Devotees wake up during Brahma Muhurta (approximately 4:30 AM) and bathe in rivers, ponds, or at home with cold water.

content.shloka:
Gange cha Yamune chaiva Godaavari Saraswati |
Narmade Sindhu Kaaveri jalasmin sannidhim kuru ||
content.meaning: O Ganga, Yamuna, Godavari, Saraswati, Narmada, Sindhu, and Kaveri — please be present in this water. This mantra is chanted before taking the Kartik bath.
content.transliteration:
Gaṅge ca Yamune caiva Godāvari Sarasvatī |
Narmade Sindhu Kāverī jalasmin sannidhiṁ kuru ||

content.shloka: After the bath, devotees apply tilak, wear clean clothes, and proceed to the temple or tulsi plant for morning worship. The bath should ideally be followed by chanting Vishnu Sahasranama or reading the Bhagavata Purana.
content.meaning: Those who are unable to bathe in rivers may bathe at home while chanting the above sacred river invocation. The spiritual merit is the same when performed with faith and devotion.
content.transliteration: After the bath, devotees apply tilak, wear clean clothes, and proceed to the temple or tulsi plant for morning worship. The bath should ideally be followed by chanting Vishnu Sahasranama or reading the Bhagavata Purana.

content.shloka:
Om apavitrah pavitro vaa sarva avasthaangato api vaa |
Yah smaret Pundareekaksham sa baahyaabhyantarah shuchih ||
content.meaning: Whether pure or impure, in whatever condition one may be, whoever remembers the lotus-eyed Lord (Vishnu) becomes pure both externally and internally. This mantra is chanted after the Kartik bath.
content.transliteration:
Om apavitraḥ pavitro vā sarvāvasthāṅgato'pi vā |
Yaḥ smaret Puṇḍarīkākṣaṁ sa bāhyābhyantaraḥ śuciḥ ||

content.shloka:
Yanmoole sarvateerthaani yannagre sarvadevataah |
Yanmadhye sarvavedaashcha tulaseem tam namaamyaham ||
content.meaning: At whose roots reside all sacred pilgrimages, at whose crown dwell all deities, in whose center reside all the Vedas — to that Tulsi, I bow in reverence.
content.transliteration:
Yanmūle sarvatīrthāni yannagre sarvadevatāḥ |
Yanmadhye sarvavedāśca tulasīṁ taṁ namāmyaham ||

content.shloka: Tulsi (Holy Basil) holds a supreme position in Kartik worship. She is considered the beloved of Lord Vishnu. No worship of Vishnu is complete without Tulsi leaves, and during Kartik, her worship becomes even more significant.
content.meaning: Devotees water the Tulsi plant daily, light a lamp near it every evening, and circumambulate it (parikrama) while chanting mantras. Tulsi is worshipped as a goddess — she is Vrinda Devi, the purest devotee of Lord Vishnu.
content.transliteration: Tulsi (Holy Basil) holds a supreme position in Kartik worship. She is considered the beloved of Lord Vishnu. No worship of Vishnu is complete without Tulsi leaves, and during Kartik, her worship becomes even more significant.

content.shloka:
Om Tulasyamritajanmasi sadaa tvam keshavapriye |
Keshavaartham chinomi tvaam varadaa bhava shobhane ||
content.meaning: O Tulsi, born from the nectar of immortality, ever dear to Lord Keshava. I pluck your leaves for the worship of Keshava. O beautiful one, bestow your blessings upon me.
content.transliteration:
Om Tulasyamṛtajanmāsi sadā tvaṁ keśavapriye |
Keśavārthaṁ cinomi tvāṁ varadā bhava śobhane ||

content.shloka: Tulsi Puja Vidhi for Kartik: 1) Clean the area around the Tulsi plant every morning. 2) Water the plant and offer kumkum and turmeric. 3) Light a ghee or sesame oil lamp near the plant every evening. 4) Perform 4 or 7 parikrama (circumambulations). 5) Chant Tulsi Stotram or the above mantras. 6) Never pluck Tulsi leaves on Ekadashi, Dwadashi, Sundays, or after sunset.
content.meaning: The month of Kartik culminates in Tulsi Vivah — the ceremonial marriage of Tulsi with Lord Vishnu (in the form of Shaligram) on the Dwadashi after Devutthani Ekadashi. This marks the beginning of the Hindu wedding season.
content.transliteration: Tulsi Puja Vidhi for Kartik: 1) Clean the area around the Tulsi plant every morning. 2) Water the plant and offer kumkum and turmeric. 3) Light a ghee or sesame oil lamp near the plant every evening. 4) Perform 4 or 7 parikrama (circumambulations). 5) Chant Tulsi Stotram or the above mantras. 6) Never pluck Tulsi leaves on Ekadashi, Dwadashi, Sundays, or after sunset.

content.shloka:
Namaami ishvaram sachchidaananda roopam
Lasat kundalam gokule bhrajamanam |
Yashoda bhiyolookhalatam dhaavanantam
Paraamrishtam atyantato drutya goopyaa ||
content.meaning: I bow to the Supreme Lord whose form is eternal bliss and knowledge, whose earrings glitter as He wanders beautifully in Gokula. He ran in fear of Mother Yashoda, dragging the mortar to which He was tied, and was finally caught by the devoted Gopi (Yashoda).
content.transliteration:
Namāmi īśvaraṁ saccidānanda rūpaṁ
Lasat kuṇḍalaṁ gokule bhrājamānam |
Yaśodā bhiyolūkhalāt dhāvamānaṁ
Parāmṛṣṭam atyantato drutya gopyā ||

content.shloka:
Rudantam muhur netra yugmam mrijantam
Karaambudvayena saatankam netram |
Muhuh shvaasa kampa trirekhaamka kantha
Sthita graivam damodaram bhakti baddham ||
content.meaning: He who was crying, repeatedly rubbing His two eyes with His lotus hands, His eyes full of fear, His neck marked with three lines and trembling with rapid breathing — that Damodara, bound by the rope of devotion, I worship.
content.transliteration:
Rudantaṁ muhur netra yugmaṁ mṛjantaṁ
Karāmbudvayena sātaṅkaṁ netram |
Muhuḥ śvāsa kampa trirekhāṅka kaṇṭha
Sthita graivaṁ dāmodaraṁ bhakti baddham ||

content.shloka:
Itidrik sva leelabhir aananda kunde
Sva ghosham nimajjantam aakhyaapayantam |
Tadiyeshita jneshu bhaktair jitatvam
Punahprema tasy tam shataavritti vande ||
content.meaning: By such playful pastimes, He immerses the people of Vraja in an ocean of bliss and reveals that He, the Supreme Lord, can be conquered only by His loving devotees. I offer my obeisances unto Him hundreds and hundreds of times.
content.transliteration:
Itīdṛk sva līlābhir ānanda kuṇḍe
Sva ghoṣaṁ nimajjantam ākhyāpayantam |
Tadīyeṣita jñeṣu bhaktair jitatvaṁ
Punaḥ prematas taṁ śatāvṛtti vande ||

content.shloka: The Damodarashtakam is sung daily during the month of Kartik while offering a ghee lamp to Lord Damodara (baby Krishna bound by a rope around His waist). This prayer, from the Padma Purana, describes the enchanting childhood pastimes of Lord Krishna in Vrindavan.
content.meaning: The name Damodara (Dama = rope, Udara = belly) refers to Krishna being bound around His waist by Mother Yashoda's love. This demonstrates that the Supreme Lord, who cannot be bound by any force in the universe, willingly submits to the pure love of His devotees.
content.transliteration: The Damodarashtakam is sung daily during the month of Kartik while offering a ghee lamp to Lord Damodara (baby Krishna bound by a rope around His waist). This prayer, from the Padma Purana, describes the enchanting childhood pastimes of Lord Krishna in Vrindavan.

content.shloka:
Varam deva moksham na mokshaa vadhim vaa
Na anyam vrine aham vareshaat apiha |
Idam te vapur naatha gopaalabalam
Sadaa me manasy aaviraastu kim anyaih ||
content.meaning: O Lord, I do not desire liberation, nor do I want anything else. All I ask is that this beautiful form of Yours as a cowherd boy may always remain manifest in my heart. What need do I have for anything else?
content.transliteration:
Varaṁ deva mokṣaṁ na mokṣāvadhiṁ vā
Na anyaṁ vṛṇe'haṁ vareśāt apīha |
Idaṁ te vapur nātha gopālabālaṁ
Sadā me manasyāvirāstu kim anyaiḥ ||

content.shloka:
Ekaadashyaam na bhunyeeta paksha yor ubha yor api |
Paapam varsha sahasrasya tad ekaadashyaatmakaanashaat ||
content.meaning: One should not eat on both Ekadashis (11th day of each lunar fortnight) in any month. Fasting on Ekadashi destroys the sins accumulated over a thousand years.
content.transliteration:
Ekādaśyāṁ na bhuñjīta pakṣayor ubhayor api |
Pāpaṁ varṣa sahasrasya tad ekādaśyātmakānaśāt ||

content.shloka: Kartik Maas contains two powerful Ekadashis: 1) Rama Ekadashi (Krishna Paksha) — dedicated to Lord Rama. 2) Devutthani / Prabodhini Ekadashi (Shukla Paksha) — the day Lord Vishnu awakens from His four-month cosmic sleep (Chaturmas).
content.meaning: Devutthani Ekadashi is the most important Ekadashi of the year. It marks the end of Chaturmas and the beginning of the auspicious season for marriages, yajnas, and other ceremonies. Devotees stay awake the entire night singing bhajans and reading scriptures.
content.transliteration: Kartik Maas contains two powerful Ekadashis: 1) Rama Ekadashi (Krishna Paksha) — dedicated to Lord Rama. 2) Devutthani / Prabodhini Ekadashi (Shukla Paksha) — the day Lord Vishnu awakens from His four-month cosmic sleep (Chaturmas).

content.shloka:
Uttishthottishtho Govinda tyaja nidram Jagatpate |
Tvayee supte jagannatha jagat suptam bhavet idam ||
content.meaning: Arise, arise O Govinda! O Lord of the Universe, leave Your sleep. When You sleep, O Lord of the World, the entire creation sleeps as well. This mantra is chanted to awaken Lord Vishnu on Devutthani Ekadashi.
content.transliteration:
Uttiṣṭhottiṣṭho Govinda tyaja nidrāṁ Jagatpate |
Tvayī supte jagannātha jagat suptaṁ bhavet idam ||

content.shloka: Ekadashi Vrat Vidhi: 1) Begin fasting from Dashami (10th day) sunset. 2) Complete fast on Ekadashi (no grains, beans, or rice). 3) Spend the day in worship, japa, and reading scriptures. 4) Stay awake at night (Jaagaran) with devotional singing. 5) Break fast (Parana) on Dwadashi at the prescribed time after sunrise.
content.meaning: Those unable to do a complete fast may observe a partial fast with fruits, milk, and root vegetables (sabudana, potato, etc.). Even partial fasting with devotion on Kartik Ekadashi grants immense spiritual merit.
content.transliteration: Ekadashi Vrat Vidhi: 1) Begin fasting from Dashami (10th day) sunset. 2) Complete fast on Ekadashi (no grains, beans, or rice). 3) Spend the day in worship, japa, and reading scriptures. 4) Stay awake at night (Jaagaran) with devotional singing. 5) Break fast (Parana) on Dwadashi at the prescribed time after sunrise.

content.shloka: Tulsi Vivah is the ceremonial marriage of the Tulsi plant (representing Goddess Vrinda/Lakshmi) with Lord Vishnu (represented by a Shaligram stone or an image of Lord Krishna). It is performed on the Dwadashi (12th day) of Kartik Shukla Paksha.
content.meaning: This sacred ceremony marks the end of the Chaturmas period and the beginning of the Hindu wedding season. No Hindu marriages are performed during Chaturmas, and Tulsi Vivah is the first wedding of the season — symbolically opening the doors for all auspicious ceremonies.
content.transliteration: Tulsi Vivah is the ceremonial marriage of the Tulsi plant (representing Goddess Vrinda/Lakshmi) with Lord Vishnu (represented by a Shaligram stone or an image of Lord Krishna). It is performed on the Dwadashi (12th day) of Kartik Shukla Paksha.

content.shloka:
Om Tulaseem kaanana yaameem vishnu bhaaryaam namaamyaham |
Yat paada padmam mahateertham namastasyai namo namah ||
content.meaning: I bow to Tulsi, who dwells in the forests, who is the consort of Lord Vishnu, whose lotus feet are the greatest pilgrimage. Salutations to her again and again.
content.transliteration:
Om Tulasīṁ kānana yāmīṁ Viṣṇu bhāryāṁ namāmyaham |
Yat pāda padmaṁ mahātīrthaṁ namastasyai namo namaḥ ||

content.shloka: Tulsi Vivah Vidhi: 1) Decorate the Tulsi plant as a bride — apply haldi, kumkum, and drape with a mini saree. 2) Place Shaligram or Krishna idol next to Tulsi as the groom. 3) Erect a small mandap (wedding canopy) with sugarcane and mango leaves. 4) Perform the wedding ceremony with Vedic mantras.
content.meaning: The ceremony includes all the traditional wedding rituals — Kanya Daan, Mangalsutra, Sindoor, and Saptapadi (seven rounds around the sacred fire). Devotees sing wedding songs and offer sweets, fruits, and flowers.
content.transliteration: Tulsi Vivah Vidhi: 1) Decorate the Tulsi plant as a bride — apply haldi, kumkum, and drape with a mini saree. 2) Place Shaligram or Krishna idol next to Tulsi as the groom. 3) Erect a small mandap (wedding canopy) with sugarcane and mango leaves. 4) Perform the wedding ceremony with Vedic mantras.

content.shloka:
Vrindaayai Tulasi devyai priyaayai Keshavaaya cha |
Krishna bhakti prade devi satyavatyai namo namah ||
content.meaning: Salutations to Vrinda, to goddess Tulsi, to the beloved of Keshava (Vishnu), to the one who grants devotion to Krishna, to the truthful one — I bow again and again.
content.transliteration:
Vṛndāyai Tulasī devyai priyāyai Keśavāya ca |
Kṛṣṇa bhakti prade devī Satyavatyai namo namaḥ ||

content.shloka: After the marriage ceremony, devotees break open a tamarind or amla (gooseberry) fruit — symbolizing the breaking of the Chaturmas restrictions. From this day onward, marriages, house-warmings, and new ventures may be undertaken.
content.meaning: Tulsi Vivah is celebrated with great enthusiasm across India, particularly in Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh. Community celebrations include mass Tulsi Vivah ceremonies, feasts, and cultural programs. It is believed that performing or witnessing Tulsi Vivah grants the same merit as performing an actual Kanya Daan (giving away a daughter in marriage).
content.transliteration: After the marriage ceremony, devotees break open a tamarind or amla (gooseberry) fruit — symbolizing the breaking of the Chaturmas restrictions. From this day onward, marriages, house-warmings, and new ventures may be undertaken.

content.shloka:
Om Damodaraya Vidmahe Vasudevaya Dheemahi |
Tanno Krishna Prachodayaat ||
content.meaning: We know Damodara (Krishna bound by rope), we meditate upon Vasudeva. May Lord Krishna inspire and illuminate us. This is the Damodara Gayatri, the principal mantra of Kartik Maas.
content.transliteration:
Om Dāmodarāya Vidmahe Vāsudevāya Dhīmahi |
Tanno Kṛṣṇaḥ Pracodayāt ||

content.shloka:
Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya Namah |
Om Damodaraya Namah |
Om Govindaya Namah |
Om Madhavaya Namah ||
content.meaning: Salutations to Lord Vasudeva, Damodara, Govinda, and Madhava. These names of Lord Vishnu/Krishna are chanted daily during Kartik for spiritual merit and divine grace.
content.transliteration:
Om Namo Bhagavate Vāsudevāya Namaḥ |
Om Dāmodarāya Namaḥ |
Om Govindāya Namaḥ |
Om Mādhavāya Namaḥ ||

content.shloka:
Kaartike yah hareh poojaam kuryaat preetena chetasaa |
Tasya punyaphalam vakshye shrinu paarvati sundari ||
content.meaning: O beautiful Parvati, listen — I shall describe the meritorious fruit that awaits the one who performs worship of Lord Hari with a loving heart during the month of Kartik.
content.transliteration:
Kārtike yaḥ Hareḥ pūjāṁ kuryāt prītena cetasā |
Tasya puṇyaphalaṁ vakṣye śṛṇu Pārvatī sundarī ||

content.shloka: Daily Kartik Schedule: Morning — Bathe before sunrise, chant 'Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya' 108 times. Noon — Read one chapter of Bhagavata Purana. Evening — Light a ghee lamp at Tulsi, sing Damodarashtakam. Night — Chant Vishnu Sahasranama before sleeping.
content.meaning: Consistent spiritual practice throughout Kartik Maas transforms the devotee's consciousness and draws the special grace of Lord Vishnu. Even those who cannot perform elaborate rituals can gain immense merit by simply chanting the Lord's names with love and devotion.
content.transliteration: Daily Kartik Schedule: Morning — Bathe before sunrise, chant 'Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya' 108 times. Noon — Read one chapter of Bhagavata Purana. Evening — Light a ghee lamp at Tulsi, sing Damodarashtakam. Night — Chant Vishnu Sahasranama before sleeping.
